# Gota Framework 💧

> Minimalist, zero-dependency Go web micro-framework built around the REPR Design Pattern (Request-Endpoint-Response) with native interactive API documentation powered by Scalar and OpenAPI 3.1.

This document is the definitive specification, API reference, and rulebook for the **Gota** web framework in Go. Because Gota has deliberate design choices and fail-fast runtime checks, strictly follow the signatures, struct tags, and constraints documented here rather than guessing or borrowing idioms from Gin, Echo, Fiber, or Chi.

---

## 1. Overview & Core Philosophy

- **Module & Import**: `github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota`
  - Import **only** `github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota` in application code. All core types (`App`, `Context`, `Config`, `ServerConfig`, `Route`, `RouteGroup`, `RouteDoc`, `HandlerFunc`, `MiddlewareFunc`, `Map`, `Empty`, `HTTPError`, `ErrorResponse`, `ValidationError`, `OpenAPISecurityScheme`, etc.) are re-exported as type aliases on the root `gota` package.
- **Zero External Dependencies**: Built 100% on the Go standard library (`net/http`, `reflect`, `encoding/json`, `log/slog`, `sync`, `crypto/*`).
- **Standard `net/http.Handler`**: `*gota.App` implements `http.Handler` (`app.ServeHTTP(w, r)`), so it works directly with `httptest`, `http.Server`, or standard `net/http` tooling.
- **Go Version**: Requires **Go 1.26+**.

---

## 2. Application Bootstrap & Configuration

`gota.New` accepts **exactly one `gota.Config` struct** (it is **not** variadic):

```go
package main

import (
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/gota"
)

func main() {
	// Pass gota.Config{} to use all defaults, or customize fields as needed:
	app := gota.New(gota.Config{
		Title:              "My API",          // Default: "Gota API"
		Version:            "1.0.0",           // Default: "1.0.0"
		Description:        "REST API built with Gota REPR pattern",
		DocsURL:            "/docs",           // Default: "/docs"
		OpenAPIURL:         "/openapi.json",   // Default: "/openapi.json"
		ScalarTheme:        gota.ThemeFastify, // Default: gota.ThemeFastify
		ScalarLayout:       "classic",         // Default: "classic" ("classic" or "modern")
		DisableDocs:        false,             // Set true to disable /docs and /openapi.json routes
		MaxBodyBytes:       10 << 20,          // Default: 10 MiB (negative value disables limit)
		MaxMultipartMemory: 32 << 20,          // Default: 32 MiB RAM for multipart parsing (negative disables limit)
		TrustProxyHeaders:  false,             // true ONLY behind a trusted reverse proxy (X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP)
		ReadTimeout:        30 * time.Second,  // Default: 30s (negative disables; ReadHeaderTimeout is fixed at 10s)
		WriteTimeout:       30 * time.Second,  // Default: 30s (negative disables; automatically lifted for streams)
		IdleTimeout:        120 * time.Second, // Default: 120s (negative disables)
		SilenceTagWarnings: false,             // Set true to suppress non-fatal startup validation tag warnings
		// Servers:         []gota.ServerConfig{{URL: "https://api.example.com", Description: "Production"}},
		// SecuritySchemes: map[string]gota.OpenAPISecurityScheme{"ApiKey": {Type: "apiKey", In: "header", Name: "X-API-Key"}},
		// ScalarScriptURL: "/static/scalar.js",
		// ScalarSRI:       "sha384-...",
	})

	// Global Middlewares — MUST be registered BEFORE any routes or groups!
	app.Use(gota.RequestID())  // RFC 4122 UUID v4 in X-Request-ID header & ctx.RequestID()
	app.Use(gota.SlogLogger()) // Structured log/slog logger (or gota.Logger() for stdlib log)
	app.Use(gota.Recover())    // Catches handler panics inside the middleware chain -> 500 JSON
	app.Use(gota.CORS())       // Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

	// Start server with Graceful Shutdown (catches os.Interrupt / SIGTERM, 10s drain timeout)
	log.Fatal(app.ListenGraceful(":3000"))
}
```

### Server Lifecycle Methods on `*gota.App`

- `app.Listen(addr string) error`: Starts the HTTP server (`":3000"`, `"3000"`, or `"127.0.0.1:3000"`).
- `app.ListenGraceful(addr string, stopSignals ...os.Signal) error`: Starts the server and gracefully drains connections (10s timeout) on `os.Interrupt` / `syscall.SIGTERM` (or custom signals).
- `app.Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error`: Gracefully shuts down a running server started via `Listen`.
- `app.ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)`: Dispatches a request directly (ideal for `httptest`).
- `app.Server() *http.Server`, `app.Config() gota.Config`, `app.Router() *core.Router`.

### Available `ScalarTheme` Constants

`gota.ThemeFastify` (default), `gota.ThemeDefault`, `gota.ThemeAlternate`, `gota.ThemeMoon`, `gota.ThemePurple`, `gota.ThemeSolarized`, `gota.ThemeBluePlanet`, `gota.ThemeDeepSpace`, `gota.ThemeSaturn`, `gota.ThemeKepler`, `gota.ThemeElysiaJS`, `gota.ThemeMars`, `gota.ThemeLaserwave`, `gota.ThemeNone`.

### Scalar Script Pinning & Subresource Integrity (SRI)

By default, `/docs` loads Scalar from a pinned CDN URL with Subresource Integrity (`gota.DefaultScalarCDN`, `gota.DefaultScalarSRI`, `gota.DefaultScalarVersion`; helper `gota.ScalarCDNURL(version)` builds a jsDelivr URL for another version).
To self-host or use a custom CDN:
- Set `ScalarScriptURL` (and optionally `ScalarSRI`; leaving `ScalarSRI` empty skips the integrity attribute).
- `ScalarSRI` is ignored unless `ScalarScriptURL` is also set. Never pair an SRI hash with a floating `@latest` URL.

---

## 3. The REPR Pattern in Gota (Request – Endpoint – Response)

Every endpoint is modeled as a self-contained unit with three parts:
1. **Request DTO (`Req`)**: Typed struct declaring inputs across path, query, headers, form, or JSON body, plus declarative validation and OpenAPI metadata. Use `gota.Empty` (or `struct{}`) when an endpoint takes no input.
2. **Endpoint**: Handler function `func(ctx *gota.Context, req Req) (Res, error)` or struct implementing `gota.Endpoint[Req, Res]`.
3. **Response DTO (`Res`)**: Typed output serialized automatically (JSON, `204 No Content`, chunked stream, or SSE stream).

### 3.1 Request Struct Tags & Model Binding

Gota binds fields from five HTTP sources and enriches validation/OpenAPI using struct tags:

| Tag                 | Purpose / Source                                                         | Example                                          |
| :------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------- |
| `param:"name"`      | Route path parameter (`:name` or `*filepath` wildcard). **No options.**  | ``ID string `param:"id"` ``                      |
| `query:"name"`      | URL query parameter (`?name=...`). **No options.**                       | ``Page *int `query:"page"` ``                    |
| `header:"Name"`     | HTTP request header (`Req`) or outgoing response header (`Res`, pair with `json:"-"`). **No options.** | ``Token string `header:"X-Api-Key"` ``           |
| `form:"name"`       | Multipart or URL-encoded form field / file upload. **No options.**       | ``File *multipart.FileHeader `form:"file"` ``    |
| `json:"name"`       | JSON request/response body field (standard `encoding/json` options ok).  | ``Title string `json:"title,omitempty"` ``       |
| `validate:"rules"`  | Declarative validation rules (comma-separated); also exported to OpenAPI 3.1 JSON Schema (`minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `enum`, `format`). | ``Email string `json:"email" validate:"required,email"` `` |
| `msg:"messages"`    | Custom validation error message(s) (`fallback` or `rule:text\|rule:text`). | ``Name string `json:"name" validate:"required,min=3" msg:"required:Name required\|min:Too short"` `` |
| `message:"text"`    | Alias for `msg`.                                                         | ``Age int `json:"age" validate:"min=18" message:"Must be 18+"` `` |
| `doc:"description"` | OpenAPI description (works on `param`, `query`, `header`, `form`, `json`). | ``Q string `query:"q" doc:"Search term"` ``     |
| `example:"val"`     | OpenAPI example (works on `param`, `query`, `header`, `form`, `json`).   | ``Email string `json:"email" example:"a@b.com"` `` |
| `format:"fmt"`      | OpenAPI format hint (works on `param`, `query`, `header`, `form`, `json`). | ``Born string `json:"born" format:"date"` ``     |
| `default:"val"`     | OpenAPI default value (works on `param`, `query`, `header`, `form`, `json`).| ``Role string `json:"role" default:"member"` ``  |
| `gota:"nowarn"`     | Silences startup validation warnings on a specific field.                | ``Active bool `json:"active" validate:"required" gota:"nowarn"` `` |

> **CRITICAL — Never put `,omitempty` or options in `param`, `query`, `header`, or `form` tags**: Unlike `encoding/json`, `param`, `query`, `header`, and `form` tags only accept the field name (e.g. ``form:"notes"``). Writing ``form:"notes,omitempty"`` or ``query:"page,required"`` triggers a fail-fast startup **panic** in `validation.CheckTags` (only `json:"notes,omitempty"` supports `,omitempty`, and validation rules belong in `validate:"..."`).

#### Supported Field Types for `param`, `query`, `header`, and `form`

- **Strings**: `string`, `*string`
- **Integers**: `int`, `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64` (and pointers `*int`, etc.)
- **Floats**: `float32`, `float64` (and pointers `*float64`, etc.)
- **Booleans**: `bool`, `*bool` — accepts `"true"`, `"1"`, `"t"`, `"yes"`, `"y"` and `"false"`, `"0"`, `"f"`, `"no"`, `"n"` (case-insensitive); other strings return `400 Bad Request`.
- **Time & Custom `encoding.TextUnmarshaler`**: `time.Time`, `*time.Time` (parses `RFC3339Nano`, `RFC3339`, and `2006-01-02`), and any custom type implementing `encoding.TextUnmarshaler`.
- **Slices (`[]string`, `[]int`, `[]int64`, `[]float64`, `[]bool`, `[]time.Time`, etc.)**:
  - `query`: supports both repeated keys (`?id=1&id=2`) and comma-separated values (`?id=1,2`, trimmed).
  - `form`: collects repeated form fields (`tags=go` & `tags=web`) or comma-separated values.
  - `param` / `header`: splits comma-separated values (`a,b,c`, trimmed).
- **File Uploads (`form` tag with `multipart/form-data`)**:
  - Single file: `*multipart.FileHeader`
  - Multiple files under the same key: `[]*multipart.FileHeader`

#### Binding Precedence, Security Isolation & Errors

1. Body is parsed first according to `Content-Type` (`multipart/form-data`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, or JSON).
2. **Cross-Source Spoofing Protection**: Any field tagged with `param`, `query`, `header`, or `form` (without an explicit `json:"name"` tag) is zeroed after JSON unmarshaling and populated **exclusively** from its declared source, so a JSON body like `{"UserID": 1}` can never spoof a `header:"X-User-Id"` or `param:"id"` field.
3. **Binding Errors**: Malformed JSON or type conversion failures (e.g. `?page=abc` for an `int`) automatically return `HTTP 400 Bad Request` (`gota.ErrorResponse`). Payloads exceeding `Config.MaxBodyBytes` return `HTTP 413 Request Entity Too Large` (`gota.ErrorResponse`).

#### Embedded Structs (Reusable DTO Composition / Mixins)

Anonymous untagged embedded structs (value or pointer) are flattened across **binding, validation, and OpenAPI** just like `encoding/json`:

```go
type PaginationQuery struct {
	Page  *int `query:"page" doc:"Page number" validate:"min=1"`
	Limit *int `query:"limit" doc:"Items per page" validate:"min=1,max=100"`
}

type ListUsersRequest struct {
	PaginationQuery // Promoted: binds ?page=&limit=, validates as "page"/"limit", flattens in OpenAPI
	Role string     `query:"role" validate:"oneof=Admin,Customer"`
}
```

- Fields declared on the outer struct shadow promoted fields with the same tag/name.
- Embedded pointer structs (e.g. `*AuditHeaders`) stay `nil` when none of their fields are present in the request, while still enforcing `required` rules on any unshadowed inner fields.

---

### 3.2 Declarative & Custom Validation

#### Supported `validate` Rules

- `required`: Fails if the value is zero/empty:
  - `string`: empty or whitespace-only (`strings.TrimSpace(s) == ""` fails!).
  - `slice` / `map`: `nil` or `len == 0`.
  - `pointer` / `interface`: `nil`.
  - Primitives (`int`, `float64`, `bool`, structs like `time.Time`): Go zero value (`0`, `0.0`, `false`, `time.Time{}`).
- `min=N`: Minimum rune count (`string`), element count (`slice`), or numeric value (`int*`, `uint*`, `float*`). Supports decimals (e.g. `min=0.01`).
- `max=N`: Maximum rune count (`string`), element count (`slice`), or numeric value (`int*`, `uint*`, `float*`).
- `len=N`: Exact UTF-8 rune count (`string`) or item count (`slice`, `array`, `map`). Integer `N` only.
- `oneof=A,B,C` (or space-separated `oneof=A B C`): Exact match against allowed values (works on strings and numbers via `%v` formatting).
- `email`: Valid email address (`net/mail.ParseAddress`, containing `@` and `.`).
- `url`: Valid absolute URL with scheme and host (`net/url.ParseRequestURI`).
- `uuid`: Valid 36-char UUID (`xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`).
- `nowarn`: Suppresses startup warnings for this field.

#### Optional Fields, Zero Values & Pointers (CRITICAL)

Understand how Gota evaluates optional fields (fields **without** `required`):
- **Pointer fields (`*string`, `*int`, `*bool`, `*float64`, `*AddressDTO`)**:
  - Stay `nil` when omitted from `param`, `query`, `header`, `form`, or `json`.
  - When `nil`, **every rule except `required` is skipped**, and nil nested struct pointers are not recursed into.
  - When non-nil (even `&0`, `&false`, or `&""`), `required` passes and all other rules validate the dereferenced value.
- **Non-pointer fields (`string`, `int`, `bool`, `AddressDTO`)**:
  - Default to Go's zero value (`""`, `0`, `false`) when omitted.
  - `email`, `url`, `uuid`, and string `oneof` skip empty strings `""`.
  - **`min=N`, `len=N`, and numeric `oneof` DO NOT skip zero values on non-pointer fields!** For example, an omitted ``Code string `json:"code" validate:"len=6"` `` has value `""` (length 0) and **will fail `len=6`**. Use ``Code *string `json:"code" validate:"len=6"` `` whenever the field is optional!
  - **Non-pointer nested structs** (`Address AddressDTO`) are **always** recursed into. If `Address` itself is optional but its inner fields have `validate:"required"`, make it a pointer: ``Address *AddressDTO `json:"address,omitempty"` ``.
  - **Primitives with `required`**: Because `0` and `false` are Go zero values, `validate:"required"` on `int` or `bool` rejects `0` and `false`. Use `*int` or `*bool` with `validate:"required"` when `0` or `false` are valid inputs.

#### Recursive Struct & Slice Validation

Nested structs (`Address AddressDTO`, `*AddressDTO`) and slices of structs (`Items []ItemDTO`, `[]*ItemDTO`) are validated automatically without any `dive` tag. Error keys preserve full paths (e.g. `"address.street"`, `"items[0].price"`). Standard library structs (`time.Time`, `multipart.FileHeader`, `net/*`, `io/*`) are not recursed into.

#### Fail-Fast Startup Tag Checks & Warnings

At route registration, `WrapEndpoint` runs `validation.CheckTags`:
- **Intentional Panics**: Unsupported tags like `path:"id"`, unknown validation rules (e.g. `requried`, `gte=5`, `lte=10`, `length=5`, `dive`, `isdefault`), bad rule parameters (`min=abc`), or `msg` referencing undeclared rules **panic immediately at startup** with corrective suggestions.
- **Startup Warnings**: Non-fatal warnings are logged once per type for `validate:"omitempty"` (no-op in Gota) and `validate:"required"` on non-pointer numeric/bool primitives. Silence per-field with `validate:"...,nowarn"` or `gota:"nowarn"`, or globally with `Config{SilenceTagWarnings: true}` or `gota.SilenceTagWarnings(true)`.

#### Custom Error Messages (`msg` / `message` Tags)

1. **Single fallback message for any failed rule on the field**:
   ```go
   Age int `json:"age" validate:"min=18" msg:"You must be at least 18 years old."`
   ```
2. **Per-rule messages separated by `|`** (`{field}` expands to the field's property path):
   ```go
   Name string `json:"name" validate:"required,min=3" msg:"required:{field} is mandatory|min:{field} must have 3+ chars"`
   ```

#### Custom Business Validation (`Validator` & `ContextValidator`)

A request struct (or any nested struct) can implement **one** of these two methods (use `*gota.Context`, which is an alias for `*core.Context`):

```go
// Option A: Context-free custom validation
func (r *CreateOrderRequest) Validate() error {
	if r.EndDate.Before(r.StartDate) {
		return errors.New("endDate must be after startDate")
	}
	return nil
}

// Option B: Context-aware validation (access headers, auth claims, store values)
func (r *CreateOrderRequest) Validate(ctx *gota.Context) error {
	if ctx.Header("X-Tenant-ID") == "" {
		return errors.New("missing X-Tenant-ID header")
	}
	return nil
}
```

- Root struct custom validation errors are added under `"_general"`.
- Nested struct custom validation errors are added under that nested field's path (e.g. `"shippingAddress"`).

---

### 3.3 Response Types, File Uploads & Streaming

| Return Type (`Res`)                    | Behavior & OpenAPI Representation                                                        |
| :------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Struct / Slice / `gota.Map` / Generic  | Serialized as `application/json` with `200 OK` (or the status set via `.Status(code)` / `ctx.Status(code)`). Named structs become `$ref` entries in `components.schemas` (generics like `Page[User]` sanitize to `Page_User`); `time.Time` -> `date-time`, `[]byte` -> `byte`. |
| `gota.Empty` (or `struct{}`)           | Returns `HTTP 204 No Content` with an empty body (`return gota.Empty{}, nil`).           |
| `gota.StreamFunc` (or `gota.Streamer`) | Lifts server `WriteTimeout` and streams chunked bytes (`application/octet-stream`).      |
| `gota.SSEStream`                       | Lifts server `WriteTimeout` and streams `gota.SSEvent` items as `text/event-stream`.     |

> **Declarative Response Headers (`Res`)**: Any field on a response struct tagged with ``header:"Header-Name" json:"-"`` (and optional `doc:"..."` / `validate:"..."`) is automatically written as an HTTP response header before body serialization (when non-empty) and documented under `responses[status].headers` in OpenAPI 3.1. Always include `json:"-"` so `encoding/json` does not also serialize that field into the JSON body:
> ```go
> type CreateItemResponse struct {
> 	Location string `header:"Location" json:"-" doc:"URI of the created resource"`
> 	ID       int    `json:"id"`
> }
> ```

#### Example 1: Multipart File Upload (`*multipart.FileHeader` & `[]*multipart.FileHeader`)

```go
type UploadReceiptRequest struct {
	OrderID     string                  `param:"orderId" validate:"required"`
	Receipt     *multipart.FileHeader   `form:"receipt" doc:"Main receipt (PDF/PNG)" validate:"required"`
	Attachments []*multipart.FileHeader `form:"attachments" doc:"Optional extra files"`
	Notes       string                  `form:"notes" doc:"Optional notes"` // NO ,omitempty on form tags!
}

type UploadReceiptResponse struct {
	Filename string `json:"filename"`
	Size     int64  `json:"size"`
	Notes    string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
}

gota.Post(app, "/api/orders/:orderId/receipt", func(ctx *gota.Context, req UploadReceiptRequest) (UploadReceiptResponse, error) {
	file, err := req.Receipt.Open()
	if err != nil {
		return UploadReceiptResponse{}, gota.BadRequest("Failed to open uploaded file")
	}
	defer file.Close()

	return UploadReceiptResponse{
		Filename: req.Receipt.Filename,
		Size:     req.Receipt.Size,
		Notes:    req.Notes,
	}, nil
}).
	Summary("Upload order receipt").
	Tags("Orders")
```

> **Multipart memory**: `Config.MaxMultipartMemory` (default 32 MiB) caps how much multipart data stays in RAM before spilling to temp files; total payload size is still capped by `Config.MaxBodyBytes` (default 10 MiB — raise `MaxBodyBytes` when accepting uploads larger than 10 MiB!). To override multipart RAM per-route, call `ctx.SetMaxMultipartMemory(bytes)` in a middleware (before automatic REPR binding runs).

#### Example 2: Server-Sent Events (`gota.SSEStream`)

```go
type TrackOrderRequest struct {
	OrderID string `param:"orderId" validate:"required"`
}

gota.Get(app, "/api/orders/:orderId/track", func(ctx *gota.Context, req TrackOrderRequest) (gota.SSEStream, error) {
	events := make(chan gota.SSEvent)
	go func() {
		defer close(events)
		// Always respect client disconnect via ctx.Request.Context().Done()
		select {
		case <-ctx.Request.Context().Done():
			return
		case events <- gota.SSEvent{Event: "order_status", Data: gota.Map{"status": "Processing"}}:
		}
	}()
	return gota.SSEStream{Events: events}, nil
}).
	Summary("Stream order updates via SSE").
	Tags("Orders")
```

*(Note: `SSEvent.Data` writes `string` and `[]byte` directly, and JSON-marshals any other Go value.)*

#### Example 3: Chunked Byte Streaming (`gota.StreamFunc`)

```go
gota.Get(app, "/api/export", func(ctx *gota.Context, _ gota.Empty) (gota.StreamFunc, error) {
	return func(c *gota.Context) error {
		c.SetHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-ndjson")
		i := 0
		return c.Stream(func(w io.Writer) bool {
			if i >= 3 {
				return false // stop streaming
			}
			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "{\"row\":%d}\n", i)
			i++
			return true // flush chunk and continue
		})
	}, nil
})
```

---

## 4. Route Registration, Groups & Routing Rules

### 4.1 Function-Based REPR Endpoints

Use top-level generic functions `gota.Get`, `gota.Post`, `gota.Put`, `gota.Patch`, `gota.Delete`:

```go
gota.Post(app, "/api/users", func(ctx *gota.Context, req CreateUserRequest) (UserResponse, error) {
	return UserResponse{ID: 1, Name: req.Name, Email: req.Email}, nil
}).
	Summary("Create user").
	Description("Registers a new user account.").
	Tags("Users").
	Status(http.StatusCreated) // Changes default 200 to 201 in both HTTP response and OpenAPI!
```

### 4.2 Struct-Based REPR Endpoints (`gota.Endpoint[Req, Res]`)

Recommended for vertical-slice architecture and dependency injection:

```go
type GetUserEndpoint struct {
	DB *sql.DB
}

func (e *GetUserEndpoint) Handle(ctx *gota.Context, req GetUserRequest) (UserResponse, error) {
	user, err := findUser(ctx.Request.Context(), e.DB, req.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return UserResponse{}, gota.NotFound("User not found")
	}
	return user, nil
}

// Register with gota.HandleEndpoint:
gota.HandleEndpoint(app, http.MethodGet, "/api/users/:id", &GetUserEndpoint{DB: db}).
	Summary("Get user by ID").
	Tags("Users")
```

### 4.3 Route Groups & Modular `gota.RouterTarget`

Both `*gota.App` and `*gota.RouteGroup` implement `gota.RouterTarget`, allowing feature packages to accept either:

```go
func RegisterOrderRoutes(target gota.RouterTarget, store *Store) {
	gota.Get(target, "/orders", listOrdersHandler).Tags("Orders")
	gota.Get(target, "/orders/:orderId", getOrderHandler).Tags("Orders")
}

// Prefix group:
v1 := app.Group("/api/v1")
v1.Use(gota.JWT(secret)) // Group middlewares MUST be added before registering routes on the group!
RegisterOrderRoutes(v1, store)

// Empty-prefix group (applies middleware to a subset of routes without adding a URL prefix):
protected := app.Group("")
protected.Use(gota.JWT(secret))
```

### 4.4 Path Parameters, Wildcards & Router Constraints

- **Named parameters (`:param`)**: Matches a single path segment (e.g. `/users/:userId/posts/:postId` -> ``param:"userId"``, ``param:"postId"``).
- **Wildcards (`*name`)**: Must be the **final** segment of a route; captures all remaining segments joined by `/` (e.g. `/files/*filepath` matching `/files/a/b/c.pdf` binds `"a/b/c.pdf"` to ``Filepath string `param:"filepath"` `` and documents `{filepath}` in OpenAPI). Always name wildcards (`*filepath`) rather than bare `*`.
- **Consistent Parameter Names Within Same Method**: Never register conflicting parameter names at the same segment position for the **same** HTTP method (e.g. `GET /users/:id` and `GET /users/:userId/posts` panics at startup). Across different HTTP methods, automatic `OPTIONS` routes reuse existing parameter nodes, though using consistent parameter names (e.g. `:userId` everywhere) is still recommended for clean OpenAPI paths.
- **Duplicate Routes**: Registering the exact same `METHOD /path` twice panics at startup.
- **Automatic `OPTIONS` & `405 Method Not Allowed`**: Every non-`OPTIONS` route automatically gets a hidden `OPTIONS` handler (`204 No Content`) wrapped in base middlewares for CORS preflights. Requests to an existing path with an unregistered HTTP method return `405 Method Not Allowed` with the `Allow` header. Unmatched paths return `404 Not Found` (global middlewares still run on `404` and `405`).

---

## 5. Middlewares (Built-in & Custom)

### 5.1 Built-in Middlewares

```go
// 1. Correlation Request ID (validates incoming header [1..128 safe chars] or generates UUID v4)
app.Use(gota.RequestID()) // Optional: gota.RequestID(gota.RequestIDOptions{Header: "X-Correlation-ID", Generator: fn})

// 2. Logging (choose one)
app.Use(gota.SlogLogger()) // Optional: gota.SlogLogger(gota.SlogLoggerOptions{Logger: customSlog})
app.Use(gota.Logger())     // Standard log.Printf logger

// 3. Panic Recovery (logs stacktrace and returns 500 ErrorResponse JSON)
app.Use(gota.Recover())

// 4. CORS (default allows "*", common methods/headers, MaxAge 86400s)
app.Use(gota.CORS(gota.CORSOptions{
	AllowOrigins:     []string{"https://app.example.com"}, // MUST NOT be "*" when AllowCredentials is true!
	AllowMethods:     []string{"GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS"},
	AllowHeaders:     []string{"Origin", "Content-Type", "Accept", "Authorization"},
	ExposeHeaders:    []string{"X-Request-ID"},
	AllowCredentials: true,
	MaxAge:           86400,
}))

// 5. In-Memory Token Bucket Rate Limiter (returns 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After)
app.Use(gota.RateLimiter(gota.RateLimiterOptions{
	Max:    100,             // Default: 60 requests
	Window: 1 * time.Minute, // Default: 1 minute (keyed by ctx.ClientIP() unless KeyFunc is set)
}))

// 6. Constant-Time HTTP Basic Auth (automatically documents BasicAuth in OpenAPI 3.1)
adminGroup.Use(gota.BasicAuth("admin", os.Getenv("ADMIN_PASS"), gota.BasicAuthOptions{
	Realm: "Admin Area", // Optional: Validator func(user, pass string) bool
}))
```

### 5.2 Writing Custom Middlewares (`gota.MiddlewareFunc`)

Gota does **not** use `ctx.Next()`. A `gota.MiddlewareFunc` wraps a `gota.HandlerFunc` (`func(ctx *gota.Context) error`):

```go
func RequireRole(role string) gota.MiddlewareFunc {
	return func(next gota.HandlerFunc) gota.HandlerFunc {
		return func(ctx *gota.Context) error {
			claims, ok := gota.JWTClaims[*CustomClaims](ctx)
			if !ok || claims.Role != role {
				return gota.Forbidden("Insufficient permissions")
			}
			// Store request-scoped data for downstream handlers:
			ctx.Set("actor_id", claims.UserID)
			return next(ctx)
		}
	}
}

// Apply globally, per-group, or per-route:
// app.Use(RequireRole("Admin"))
// adminGroup.Use(RequireRole("Admin"))
// gota.Delete(app, "/api/users/:id", deleteUser).Middleware(RequireRole("Admin"))
```

---

## 6. Error Handling & JSON Error Schemas

Gota uses **two** distinct JSON error schemas:

### 6.1 `gota.ErrorResponse` (400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 500 & `HTTPError`)

Use the 6 built-in constructors in handlers or middlewares:

```go
return Res{}, gota.BadRequest("Invalid parameters")         // 400
return Res{}, gota.Unauthorized("Authentication required")  // 401
return Res{}, gota.Forbidden("Insufficient permissions")    // 403
return Res{}, gota.NotFound("User not found")               // 404
return Res{}, gota.UnprocessableEntity("Semantic conflict") // 422 (ErrorResponse shape)
return Res{}, gota.InternalServerError("Service error")     // 500
```

For **any other HTTP status code** (e.g. `409 Conflict`, `429 Too Many Requests`, `503 Service Unavailable`), return `&gota.HTTPError` directly (there are no `gota.Conflict` or `gota.NewHTTPError` functions on the `gota` package):

```go
return Res{}, &gota.HTTPError{
	Status:  http.StatusConflict,
	Message: "Email is already registered",
}
```

Wrapped `HTTPError` values (`fmt.Errorf("step failed: %w", gota.NotFound("..."))`) are unwrapped via `errors.As` and preserve their HTTP status.

Rendered JSON (`gota.ErrorResponse`):
```json
{
  "error": "User not found",
  "status": 404,
  "requestId": "b1a2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"
}
```
*(`requestId` is automatically populated whenever `gota.RequestID()` is active or a valid `X-Request-ID` header is present.)*

### 6.2 `gota.ValidationError` (422 Struct Validation Failures)

When declarative struct tags or `Validator` / `ContextValidator` fail, Gota automatically returns `HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity` with `gota.ValidationError`:

```json
{
  "message": "validation failed",
  "errors": {
    "email": ["field email must be a valid email address"],
    "items[0].price": ["field items[0].price must be at least 0.01"],
    "_general": ["endDate must be after startDate"]
  },
  "status": 422
}
```
*(You may also return `&gota.ValidationError{Message: "validation failed", Errors: ...}` manually from a handler to produce the same 422 schema.)*

### 6.3 Sanitized 500 Protection & Custom Handlers

- **Unexpected Go errors**: Returning a non-`HTTPError` (e.g. `sql.ErrConnDone`) logs the real error internally (`gota: handler error ...`) and returns a sanitized `500` JSON `{"error":"internal server error","status":500}` so internal details never leak to clients.
- **Panics**: Panics log the full `debug.Stack()` stacktrace and return the same sanitized `500` JSON (both in `gota.Recover()` and in `App.ServeHTTP`'s outer safety net).
- **Customizing fallback handlers**: Override `app.ErrorHandler = func(ctx *gota.Context, err error) { ... }` or `app.NotFoundHandler = func(ctx *gota.Context) error { ... }` on `*gota.App`.

---

## 7. Authentication & JWT (HS256, RS256, ES256, EdDSA & KeyFunc)

Gota includes zero-dependency JWT signing, verification, PEM key parsers, `KeyFunc` key rotation, and Bearer middlewares for **HS256**, **RS256**, **ES256**, and **EdDSA (Ed25519)**. Routes or groups using Gota's JWT middlewares automatically document `BearerAuth` in OpenAPI 3.1 `components.securitySchemes`.

### 7.1 Symmetric HMAC-SHA256 (HS256)

```go
var jwtSecret = []byte(os.Getenv("JWT_SECRET")) // Never hardcode secrets!

type CustomClaims struct {
	UserID int    `json:"userId"`
	Role   string `json:"role"`
	Exp    int64  `json:"exp"`
}

// Sign token (optional 3rd argument sets the JOSE header "kid"):
token, err := gota.SignJWT(jwtSecret, CustomClaims{
	UserID: 42,
	Role:   "Admin",
	Exp:    time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour).Unix(),
}) // or gota.SignJWT(jwtSecret, claims, "hmac-kid-1")

// Verify standalone token (enforces exp/nbf if present; pass nil target to verify signature/time only):
var claims CustomClaims
err = gota.VerifyJWT(jwtSecret, tokenString, &claims)
```

### 7.2 Protecting Routes & Extracting Claims

```go
protected := app.Group("/api")
protected.Use(gota.JWT(jwtSecret, gota.JWTOptions{
	RequireExp: true, // Rejects tokens that omit a positive 'exp' claim
	// CRITICAL: ClaimsFactory MUST return a POINTER (&CustomClaims{}), NOT a value!
	ClaimsFactory: func() any { return &CustomClaims{} },
	// ContextKey: "user", // Default is "user"
}))

gota.Get(protected, "/me", func(ctx *gota.Context, _ gota.Empty) (UserResponse, error) {
	claims, ok := gota.JWTClaims[*CustomClaims](ctx) // Also supports gota.JWTClaims[CustomClaims](ctx)
	if !ok {
		return UserResponse{}, gota.Unauthorized("Unauthorized")
	}
	return UserResponse{ID: claims.UserID}, nil
})
```

- **Without `ClaimsFactory`**: Claims decode into `map[string]any` and can be retrieved via `claims, ok := gota.JWTClaims[map[string]any](ctx)`.
- **Custom `ContextKey`**: If `ContextKey: "admin"` was set in `JWTOptions`, pass it as the second argument: `gota.JWTClaims[*CustomClaims](ctx, "admin")`.
- **Raw Token & JOSE Header**: Authenticated requests also store the raw Bearer token at `ctx.Get("jwt_token")`. Use `hdr, err := gota.ParseJWTHeader(tokenString)` to inspect `Alg`, `Typ`, and `Kid` prior to verification.

### 7.3 Asymmetric RSA (RS256), ECDSA P-256 (ES256), EdDSA (Ed25519) & Dynamic `KeyFunc`

```go
// --- RS256 (PKCS#1 / PKCS#8 private PEM; PKIX / PKCS#1 / X.509 cert public PEM) ---
rsaPriv, err := gota.ParseRSAPrivateKeyFromPEM(privPEM)
rsaPub, err := gota.ParseRSAPublicKeyFromPEM(pubPEM)

token, err := gota.SignJWTRSA(rsaPriv, claims, "kid-2026-01") // keyID is optional
err = gota.VerifyJWTRSA(rsaPub, token, &claims)
protected.Use(gota.JWTRSA(rsaPub, gota.JWTOptions{
	RequireExp:    true,
	ClaimsFactory: func() any { return &CustomClaims{} },
}))

// --- ES256 (NIST P-256 curve; SEC 1 / PKCS#8 private PEM; PKIX / X.509 cert public PEM) ---
ecPriv, err := gota.ParseECPrivateKeyFromPEM(ecPrivPEM)
ecPub, err := gota.ParseECPublicKeyFromPEM(ecPubPEM)

token, err = gota.SignJWTES256(ecPriv, claims, "apple-key-1") // 64-byte R||S RFC 7518 signature
err = gota.VerifyJWTES256(ecPub, token, &claims)
protected.Use(gota.JWTES256(ecPub, gota.JWTOptions{
	RequireExp:    true,
	ClaimsFactory: func() any { return &CustomClaims{} },
}))

// --- EdDSA (Ed25519; PKCS#8 private PEM; PKIX / X.509 cert public PEM) ---
edPriv, err := gota.ParseEdPrivateKeyFromPEM(edPrivPEM)
edPub, err := gota.ParseEdPublicKeyFromPEM(edPubPEM)

token, err = gota.SignJWTEdDSA(edPriv, claims, "ed-key-1")
err = gota.VerifyJWTEdDSA(edPub, token, &claims)
protected.Use(gota.JWTEdDSA(edPub, gota.JWTOptions{
	RequireExp:    true,
	ClaimsFactory: func() any { return &CustomClaims{} },
}))

// --- Dynamic Key Rotation by 'kid' (KeyFunc) ---
keyFunc := func(hdr gota.JWTHeader) (any, error) {
	// Return []byte (HS256), *rsa.PublicKey (RS256), *ecdsa.PublicKey (ES256), or ed25519.PublicKey (EdDSA)
	return lookupKeyByKid(hdr.Kid)
}
err = gota.VerifyJWTWithKeyFunc(keyFunc, token, &claims)
protected.Use(gota.JWTWithKeyFunc(keyFunc, gota.JWTOptions{
	RequireExp:    true,
	ClaimsFactory: func() any { return &CustomClaims{} },
}))
```

---

## 8. Fluent Route Metadata & Reverse URL Lookup

Every route registration (`gota.Get`, `gota.HandleEndpoint`, `app.Get`, etc.) returns `*gota.Route`:

```go
gota.Get(app, "/api/users/:id", getUserHandler).
	Summary("Get user by ID").
	Description("Fetches a single user profile.").
	Tags("Users").
	Status(http.StatusOK).                                           // Overrides default success status & OpenAPI code
	Response(http.StatusNotFound, gota.ErrorResponse{}, "Not found"). // Documents extra OpenAPI status codes
	Middleware(auditMiddleware).                                     // Appends route-specific middleware(s)
	Name("users.show")                                               // Registers route name for app.URLFor
	// Also available on *gota.Route (and .BearerAuth() / .Security(...) on *gota.RouteGroup):
	// .BearerAuth()                                                 // Documents BearerAuth in OpenAPI & Scalar (auto-applied by gota.JWT*)
	// .Security("BearerAuth")                                       // Documents custom/named security scheme(s)
	// .Deprecated()                                                 // Marks deprecated in OpenAPI
	// .Hidden()                                                     // Hides route from OpenAPI & Scalar UI
	// .Body(model, desc...), .Query(name, model, desc...), .Header(name, model, desc...) // Manual docs for low-level routes
```

**Reverse URL Lookup (`app.URLFor`)**:
Replaces `:param` and `*wildcard` segments; any extra keys in the map are automatically URL-encoded as query parameters:

```go
url, err := app.URLFor("users.show", map[string]string{
	"id":  "42",
	"tab": "activity",
})
// url == "/api/users/42?tab=activity"
```

---

## 9. `gota.Context` Reference & Low-Level Escape Hatch

### 9.1 Low-Level Non-REPR Routes

For redirects, plain-text healthchecks, webhooks needing raw bytes, or custom responses without DTOs, use `app.Get` / `Post` / `Put` / `Patch` / `Delete` / `RegisterRoute` (or the same methods on `*gota.RouteGroup`) with `func(ctx *gota.Context) error`:

```go
app.Get("/", func(ctx *gota.Context) error {
	return ctx.Redirect("/docs") // Default 302 Found; pass optional status e.g. ctx.Redirect("/docs", http.StatusMovedPermanently)
}).Hidden()

app.Get("/healthz", func(ctx *gota.Context) error {
	return ctx.Send("OK")
}).Hidden()
```

### 9.2 `*gota.Context` Fields & Methods

*(Note method casing: **`ctx.Json(...)`** and **`ctx.BindJson(...)`**, NOT `ctx.JSON`!)*

- **Underlying `net/http`**:
  - `ctx.Request` (`*http.Request` — use `ctx.Request.Context()` for `context.Context`!)
  - `ctx.ResponseWriter` (`http.ResponseWriter`)
  - `ctx.Params` (`map[string]string`)
- **Request-Scoped Key-Value Store (thread-safe)**:
  - `ctx.Set(key string, val any)`
  - `ctx.Get(key string) (any, bool)`
- **Input Helpers** *(prefer REPR DTO tags in REPR endpoints)*:
  - Path: `ctx.Param(name) string`, `ctx.HasParam(name) bool`, `ctx.ParamInt(name, def) int`, `ctx.ParamInt64(name, def) int64`
  - Query: `ctx.Query(name) string`, `ctx.QueryDefault(name, def) string`, `ctx.QueryInt(name, def) int`, `ctx.QueryBool(name, def) bool`
  - Headers & Cookies: `ctx.Header(name) string`, `ctx.Cookie(name) (*http.Cookie, error)`
  - Client & Correlation: `ctx.ClientIP() string`, `ctx.RequestID() string`
  - Body & Forms: `ctx.Body() ([]byte, error)` *(cached, safe to call multiple times)*, `ctx.BindJson(targetPtr) error`, `ctx.Form(name) string`, `ctx.FormFile(name) (*multipart.FileHeader, error)`, `ctx.MultipartForm() (*multipart.Form, error)`, `ctx.MaxMultipartMemory() int64`, `ctx.SetMaxMultipartMemory(limit int64)`
- **Response Helpers**:
  - Status & Headers: `ctx.Status(code int) *gota.Context`, `ctx.StatusCode() int`, `ctx.StatusExplicit() bool`, `ctx.SetHeader(key, val string) *gota.Context`, `ctx.SetCookie(cookie *http.Cookie) *gota.Context`, `ctx.Written() bool`
  - Writers: `ctx.Json(data any) error`, `ctx.Send(text string) error`, `ctx.SendBytes(data []byte) error`, `ctx.NoContent() error`, `ctx.Redirect(url string, code ...int) error`
  - Streaming: `ctx.Stream(step func(w io.Writer) bool) error`, `ctx.SSEvent(event string, data any) error`

---

## 10. Testing Gota Applications

Because `*gota.App` implements `http.Handler`, test endpoints directly in-memory with `net/http/httptest` (no TCP ports or `time.Sleep` needed):

```go
func TestCreateUser(t *testing.T) {
	app := gota.New(gota.Config{DisableDocs: true, SilenceTagWarnings: true})
	gota.Post(app, "/users", createUserHandler).Status(http.StatusCreated)

	body := strings.NewReader(`{"name":"Jane Doe","email":"jane@example.com"}`)
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/users", body)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	app.ServeHTTP(rec, req)

	if rec.Code != http.StatusCreated {
		t.Fatalf("expected 201, got %d: %s", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
	}
}
```

---

## 11. Critical Rules & Anti-Patterns for AI Agents

> [!CAUTION]
> **STRICT CHECKLIST — VIOLATING THESE CAUSES COMPILE ERRORS, STARTUP PANICS, OR SILENT BUGS:**

1. ❌ **Do NOT omit `gota.Config` or pass variadic args**: `gota.New()` does not compile. Always pass one struct: `gota.New(gota.Config{})`.
2. ❌ **Do NOT call generic methods on `app` or `group`**: `app.Get[Req, Res](...)` is invalid Go. Always use `gota.Get(app, path, fn)`, `gota.Post(group, path, fn)`, or `gota.HandleEndpoint(target, method, path, ep)`.
3. ❌ **Do NOT call `app.Use` or `group.Use` AFTER registering routes**: Middlewares bind at route registration time; calling `Use` late triggers an intentional **panic**.
4. ❌ **Do NOT use `path:"id"`**: Gota uses ``param:"id"`` for path parameters. `path:"id"` triggers an intentional startup **panic**.
5. ❌ **Do NOT add `,omitempty` or options to `param`, `query`, `header`, or `form` tags**: Writing ``form:"notes,omitempty"`` or ``query:"page,required"`` triggers an intentional startup **panic**. Only `json:"notes,omitempty"` supports `,omitempty`, and validation rules belong in `validate:"..."`.
6. ❌ **Do NOT use non-pointer optional fields with `min=N`, `len=N`, or optional nested structs**: Zero values (`""`, `0`) fail `min`/`len`, and non-pointer nested structs are always recursed into. Use pointer types (`*string`, `*int`, `*AddressDTO`) for optional constrained fields, and `*int` / `*bool` when `0` or `false` must pass `validate:"required"`.
7. ❌ **Do NOT mix different path param names at the same URL position for the same HTTP method**: Registering `GET /orders/:id` and `GET /orders/:orderId/items` **panics** at startup. Use `:orderId` consistently across all routes.
8. ❌ **Do NOT return a non-pointer from `JWTOptions.ClaimsFactory`**: Always write `ClaimsFactory: func() any { return &CustomClaims{} }`. Returning a value (`CustomClaims{}`) makes `json.Unmarshal` fail and rejects all tokens with `401`.
9. ❌ **Do NOT invent non-existent Gota methods or helpers**:
   - There is **no** `ctx.Next()` — custom middlewares use `func(next gota.HandlerFunc) gota.HandlerFunc`.
   - Use `ctx.Json(...)` and `ctx.BindJson(...)`, **not** `ctx.JSON(...)`.
   - Only 6 error constructors exist (`BadRequest`, `Unauthorized`, `Forbidden`, `NotFound`, `UnprocessableEntity`, `InternalServerError`). For other statuses (409, 429, etc.), return `&gota.HTTPError{Status: code, Message: msg}`.
   - Do **not** use `go-playground/validator` rules (`gte`, `lte`, `gt`, `lt`, `dive`, `omitempty`); Gota panics on unknown rules (use `min`/`max`, automatic recursion, and pointer types instead).
10. ❌ **Do NOT combine `CORSOptions{AllowCredentials: true}` with `AllowOrigins: []string{"*"}`**: Gota intentionally **panics**; list explicit origins instead.
11. ❌ **Do NOT accept privilege fields (`role`, `isAdmin`, `permissions`) in public request DTOs**: Always derive identity and roles server-side from verified JWT claims.
